framework.basis: Internal judgement of the AI Tathastu team, informed by the public references listed below (certification exam guides, occupational databases, university syllabi and official documentation). Not an industry standard, employer requirement or job-market dataset; weights and expected levels are our own and can be challenged.

evidenceForLevel.Foundational: Any use of the skill in your own described work or in a repository.
evidenceForLevel.Working: Code that uses it in at least one public repository, or your own descriptions of it in two or more projects or jobs (the highest level self-described work can reach).
evidenceForLevel.Proficient: Code that uses it in two or more repositories, or one repository with tests, CI or a documented evaluation, or a platform assessment of 3 stars or more.
evidenceForLevel.Advanced: Code that uses it in three or more repositories plus tests, CI, documented evaluation or work experience, or a platform assessment of 4 stars or more. Topics and descriptions alone never reach Advanced.

tiers.required: Needed for the role. Decides alignment; needs evidence we can check ourselves.
tiers.supporting: Strengthens a candidate. Never holds back alignment; described work counts.
tiers.specialisation: Part of a named specialisation track. Optional; shown when it matches your goals or project.

framework.alignmentRules: not_enough_evidence: nothing to read yet, or no competency in the framework has any evidence (even a claim). requirements_demonstrated: every required competency is met (expected level, demonstrated evidence). strong: every required competency has an assessed level, at least half are met, and every required competency with no required prerequisite (the foundations) is met. developing: at least one required competency is met, or at least half have an assessed level. early: anything else with some evidence. Supporting and specialisation competencies never raise the state.

framework.basis: Internal judgement of the AI Tathastu team, informed by the public references listed below (certification exam guides, occupational databases, university syllabi and official documentation). Not an industry standard, employer requirement or job-market dataset; weights and expected levels are our own and can be challenged.

evidenceForLevel.Foundational: Any use of the skill in your own described work or in a repository.
evidenceForLevel.Working: Code that uses it in at least one public repository, or your own descriptions of it in two or more projects or jobs (the highest level self-described work can reach).
evidenceForLevel.Proficient: Code that uses it in two or more repositories, or one repository with tests, CI or a documented evaluation, or a platform assessment of 3 stars or more.
evidenceForLevel.Advanced: Code that uses it in three or more repositories plus tests, CI, documented evaluation or work experience, or a platform assessment of 4 stars or more. Topics and descriptions alone never reach Advanced.

tiers.required: Needed for the role. Decides alignment; needs evidence we can check ourselves.
tiers.supporting: Strengthens a candidate. Never holds back alignment; described work counts.
tiers.specialisation: Part of a named specialisation track. Optional; shown when it matches your goals or project.

roadmap.assumption: Ordered by what each skill builds on and how central it is to your goal and project. No time estimates: they'd depend on hours we don't know you have.
